inputs: Incoming shot with an isolatable subject
Matching original-color and white alpha mattes
recipe.preparation: Continuous variant: align white and original-color alpha mattes to the incoming picture. At 30 fps, cover all five lead-in frames: white for two frames, color for three, then switch scene. No empty frame between masks. Keep each matte native and editable. For consecutive handoffs, invoke mask-glitch with ordered shots and derive one coordinated chain schedule; masks remain separate editable rows.
success_criteria: Every lead-in frame contains the white silhouette or original-color subject mask; no disappearance before the incoming scene.
White and colour masks share alpha and geometry and match the incoming picture; preserve unchanged sources and editable layers.
Verify on another incoming subject before promoting the recipe to complete.

observations: Rebuilt for the Templates card with the bobblehead, landscape 16:9: a bright library hands off to a bookshelf in directional light, then to home bookshelves with small lights, each with a still bobblehead pose in the middle of the frame (alpha PNG, no cut-out needed).
Each lead-in is 5 frames at 30 fps (2 white, 3 original colour) ending on the cut, the skill's continuous handoff default; checked frame by frame at 55-60 and 115-120.
Recreation sample is the Mask Glitch template result (1280×720, 30 fps, 180 frames). The practice contact sheet is from the earlier Pexels build (desert walker and skater) and its 9-frame lead-ins.
Continuous coverage: no empty frame between the masks and the incoming scene.
limitations: Lead-in is lengthened from the 5-frame default to 9 frames so the steps read at gallery size; continuous coverage intentionally differs from the reference pulse/off cadence.
No dedicated Mask Glitch preset; matte preparation and native layer composition remain the supported route.
